transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the release package review for 'After the Flood' ahead of the Meridian International Film Festival. I'll need each of you — rights, music, publicity, and accessibility — to walk me through your respective sign-offs so we can address any issues before I lock the package. I have the current draft release sheet in front of me: worldwide access, the cue 'Low Tide,' the working title 'River After Rain,' and optional accessibility materials. Who'd like to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue before we go any further. I confirmed with the archive this week that the license for our archival interview permits festival screening and password-protected press access only in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland. It forbids public online access and access in all other territories. The archive's signed email arrived after the last package revision, so I haven't copied the confirmation into the release sheet yet. This means the current draft's 'worldwide access' listing is not going to work — we need to correct the territories before Mara locks the package.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a music clearance issue. I confirmed with the publisher that the current cue 'Low Tide' is only cleared for 30 seconds, but our trailer segment runs 46 seconds. The alternate cue 'Northbound' is cleared for the full 46-second segment. I haven't replaced the cue name in the package yet because the editor delivered the latest cut after my clearance check, so the release sheet still lists 'Low Tide.' We need to switch the cue to 'Northbound' before Mara locks the package.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a publicity issue. I have the filmmaker's signed publicity approval, which requires the title 'After the Flood' and the credit line 'A film by Nia Okafor.' The signed approval arrived during the poster revision, so the draft release sheet still lists the working title 'River After Rain' and a generic credit. We need to update both the title and the credit line before Mara locks the package.
transcript.speaker: A4

I confirmed with the festival's access coordinator that the final submission must include open English captions and a separate audio-description track. The coordinator will reject a package containing either deliverable as optional. This requirement came in a separate accessibility email, so I haven't updated the release checklist yet — but the current draft listing accessibility materials as optional is not going to work. We need to make open English captions and a separate audio-description track mandatory deliverables before Mara locks the package.
